title: Complaint of the Session of Red Mountain Presbyterian Church vs. Evangel Presbytery
disposition_detail: The SJC sustained all four elements of the Session’s complaint and reversed Presbytery’s action under BCO 43-10. It found error in Presbytery’s rulings about the Session’s response and use of the strong-presumption standard, its handling of the commission report, and its declaration that Mrs. Walker lacked biblical divorce grounds. The SJC did not itself decide whether such grounds existed.
first_summary: Red Mountain Session challenged Presbytery’s ruling that it inadequately addressed a member’s request to declare his wife’s divorce unbiblical. The SJC sustained the complaint and reversed Presbytery, holding that the Session manifested no clear error, that Presbytery mishandled its commission report, and that its declaration and Matthew 18 instruction judged the wife without due process. The SJC did not decide whether she had biblical grounds for divorce.
summary: Red Mountain Session challenged Presbytery’s ruling that it had inadequately addressed a member’s demand to declare his wife’s divorce unbiblical, and Presbytery’s resulting declaration and Matthew 18 instruction. The SJC sustained all four issues and reversed Presbytery. It held Session’s context-sensitive ruling disclosed no clear error, use of BCO 31-2 was reasonable, Presbytery violated BCO 15-3 by allowing its commission to revise a report after floor discussion, and Presbytery judged the wife without due process. The SJC expressly did not decide whether biblical divorce grounds existed.
